title: Carrot and butter bean soup with cumin

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or a cupboard staple: carrots, onion, garlic, tinned butter beans, vegetable stock, cumin, lemon, natural yoghurt and pumpkin seeds.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at Tesco or any mainstream supermarket, and none would feel like a treat.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a saucepan, a peeler and a stick blender for soup, and the technique is simple frying, simmering and blending.

works.reason: 800g thinly sliced carrots, two tins of beans and 1.2 litres of stock make a thick soup for four, and the carrots will be soft after the 15 to 20 minute simmer.

honest_times.reason: 15 minutes hands-on is tight once you peel and slice 800g of carrots, but you can slice them while the onion softens, and 35 minutes in total fits a quick lunch.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient is used and matches its id, and the only unlisted item is an optional splash of water.

seasonal_feel.reason: Stored December carrots are clearly the point of this warming, blended soup, which suits the week before Christmas.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear and practical in plain British English, with useful cues such as 'soft enough to squash with a spoon'.

hearty_healthy.reason: Plenty of vegetables, beans for protein, and a yoghurt and toasted seed topping make it a filling lunch a family would want again.
